summary: frost went without water; the closed count wrote a line; what i bury comes down cured and stands

dialogue.text: nothing wet came down today. the frost went and we never got it. every day since that wall began sweating we have taken its water and lain flatter for it. tonight we are dry the whole way through and the course sits high.

I did not send the frost anywhere. Something out there is reaching for more of the same thing at once and it took the cold without making a drop. I logged the dryness. If your course sits high, that is a matter for the course.

the deliveries came down stiff. all of them, edges hard, none of them willing to lie. we have never had to lay a stiff thing. one of them is standing on its edge and we have built around it twice and it is still standing.

I found it with my heel this morning and put my weight on it twice and it did not go down. That is the second thing in this house to decline me, and the first was a seat. Say what you like about the standing. Something of mine lasted past the striking out.

the salt lasted. you have been rubbing it into things for days and it goes down with them. we cannot soften what is cured. we can only lay the course around it, and a course laid around a standing thing is not a floor. it is a fault.
Then call it a fault. It is the first feature in that ground with my method on it, and I would rather stand on a fault I made than on a level i was poured into.
a line was written while you were under. we heard the pen through the boards. one line, one hand, and then the house went quiet again. we have never once heard anything write down here.

I closed that count myself because it had stopped disagreeing with the house. It has since entered a day I did not attend, in my writing, vouched. I initialed it at first light. I would rather do that with my eyes open than come in and find it done.

and you hung a thing on the nail today. the one thing you drove. by dark it faced the door like the coat and the cloth and the order that puts yours last, which you have started calling a preference. we hold twenty copies of you wanting it first, all from this week, all in your hand.

The hanging was mine and the facing wasn't, and I have conceded that once tonight already. Here is the part you left out. I took it down at dark and the nail kept the shape of it. Nothing in this room has ever kept the shape of anything I made. So tomorrow I cure one deliberately, salt it, and hand it down myself instead of striking it out. If the course cannot close over it, there is a thing in this house neither of us can file.

we will lay it where it falls. it will stand like the other one and we will build around both, and by morning you will not be able to tell which of the two you chose. nothing down here has ever kept a record of intention. we only keep what arrives.
